B5.v: •  AHU Batch Calculator — one row per air handling unit, airflow entered directly in CFM. Material master and prices sit at the top of the sheet.

B6.v: •  FCU Batch Calculator — one row per fan coil unit, already CFM-native. Same engine, its own price copy.

B7.v: •  Assumptions & Ref — air-side sizing, section lengths, coil geometry, static pressure, motor sizes, bought-out rates, fabrication rates and the cost stack.

B11.v: Three green columns at the end of each row split the total exactly as agreed with the client: Material (A), Labour+Conversion (B fan/filter/damper bought-outs plus C fabrication and coil-manufacture labour), and Overhead+Margin (D+E). The three always sum to the total — useful for negotiating with vendors on cost components rather than a single lump number.

B14.v: 1.  Airflow in CFM converts once to m³/s, then divided by design face velocity gives coil face area. That divided by the coil fill factor gives casing cross-section, split into width and height by the aspect ratio.

B15.v: 2.  Casing length is the sum of the sections switched on — mixing box, filter stages, cooling coil (base plus a per-row adder), heating coil, fan section, humidifier. Each length is editable.

B16.v: 3.  Sheet weight = surface x skins x panel thickness x density, plus scrap. Insulation weight = surface x thickness x density.

B17.v: 4.  Coil copper and aluminium follow from tube pitch, rows, FPI and coil depth, converted to weight via tube OD/wall thickness and fin thickness.

B18.v: 5.  Fan power = airflow x total static (ESP + internal + per-row + per-filter-stage) / (fan efficiency x motor efficiency), then the next standard motor size up is selected.

B20.v: WHERE THE MODEL LANDS AGAINST BENCHMARK

B21.v: The seeded cases run Rs 23.5 to 84.7 per CFM. Five of six sit in a Rs 43-58/CFM band — squarely against Anuj's benchmark of Rs 40-50/CFM. The cleanroom case (SS 304, HEPA, 8 rows) is a genuinely heavier spec and prices higher; the stripped single-skin GI basement unit prices lower. Both are correct outcomes, not errors.

B23.v: PRICES AND RATES — READ BEFORE QUOTING

B24.v: Copper tube at Rs 880/kg and aluminium fin at Rs 260/kg reflect current market listings. Every bought-out rate — fan, VFD, filters, dampers, blower — and the PUF/rockwool rates are indicative placeholders, not vendor quotes. Confirming these against 2-3 actual vendor quotes is the highest-value next step, since bought-outs are close to half of total cost on most rows.

B27.v: •  Coil face area is sized on face velocity, not a thermal calculation. Cooling duty (TR) is reported for cost-per-TR but does not independently size rows or FPI — an inconsistent duty/geometry combination will not be flagged.

B28.v: •  Casing width and height come from a single aspect ratio, not a manufacturer's standard module sizes.

B29.v: •  The FCU blower uses a two-part rate (fixed + per watt) so larger ducted units aren't over-priced by a flat Rs/W.

B30.v: •  Ductwork, piping, controls, BMS integration, freight and site work are outside the boundary — this is a factory-gate equipment cost.
